about.tool: A broad-edged pen held at about 35°.
about.proportions: x-height about 5¾ nib widths; ascenders 0.37 x-heights above it, descenders 0.42 below; capitals 1.4 x-heights.
about.features: Italic's structure with blackletter's angles and weight: arches that leave the stem high up as a straight hairline and turn at a sharp peak, a lens-shaped o, a two-part a and g (the left side, a hairline up into the stem, a separate top, the stem), heads bent to the left, forked ascender heads, pointed feet. The capitals mix round (uncial-like) C, D, E, G, M, O, T with straight A, H, I, K, L, N, begun with a hairline curl and decorated with hairlines: across the round letters' left side, through M, W, X, beside the stems of H, I, K, L. Simplified: the hairlines are set a little further from the stems than on the sheet, so a copy can tell them apart; the figures (the sheet has none) are old-style.
about.history: A 20th-century calligrapher's hand: italic written with the angularity and weight of blackletter, close to the Bâtarde and the gothic cursives of the 15th and 16th centuries.
